distinguishing_features: Applies stiffness-change monitoring to a traction wire rope at the sheave bending zone rather than a gear tooth root.
Uses high-frequency torsional vibration harmonics of the rope, specifically the 3rd harmonic above 1 kHz, as the monitored observable.
Uses an existing triaxial accelerometer on the traction sheave and FFT of a high-frequency vibration stream rather than speed-corrected gear-mesh envelope demodulation.
Sets a baseline-relative 3rd-harmonic amplitude threshold over consecutive rope cycles as the alert criterion.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Provide earlier detection of incipient localized fatigue damage in a traction wire rope at the sheave bending zone, where periodic visual inspection only reveals surface wire breaks after damage has progressed.
parsed.viable_reason: The candidate's governing calculation is numerically wrong by orders of magnitude and the key 0.8 dB harmonic amplification is only assumed, with no plausible shown coupling from a 0.1 mm rope crack to the existing sheave accelerometer.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Given prior art 1's teaching of detecting early fatigue cracks through crack-induced stiffness modulation in existing vibration data, selecting rope torsional harmonics and a 3rd-harmonic threshold is a routine adaptation rather than an inventive mechanism.
